summary: T-0610 [security-debt, bug, столп4]: closes F-1 from the T-0605 security review (docs/review/T-0605.review.json) — src/http/invoke.ts::loadCallerInvokeGrants ran its OWN inline SQL (JOIN role_assignment + grant, filtered ONLY on operation='invoke') instead of the canonical getGrantsForSubject resolver every other PDP consumer uses. The inline query had NO assignment-active predicate (no confirmed_by, no validity window, no T-0605 canonical confirmed2_by/proposed_by gate) and NO grant-active predicate (no confirmed_by, no window, no T-0397 criticalGrantPredicate + confirmed2_by dual-control gate) — so an unconfirmed or expired role assignment, and a semi-confirmed (one-approver) invoke-grant (axis-b critical by construction: resource_type='effect_resource' AND operation='invoke'), were both silently treated as PDP-active. Dual-control was bypassed entirely on the one surface whose whole purpose is gating an external agent effect. Fix: loadCallerInvokeGrants now calls getGrantsForSubject(pool, tenantId, callerId, nowMs) and filters the result to operation==='invoke' in TS — the exact pattern src/db/capability-grants-dao.ts already uses. coversInvoke (the role/scope-match predicate) is untouched; only the SOURCE of grants it scans over changed. No migration (both predicates already exist and apply to existing tables).

A founder-facing LIVE_PROOF click-through does not apply here: there is no new UI surface, and the invoke/agent-runtime endpoints (POST /api/invoke/request|command) are an agent-to-agent API with no dedicated screen to click through in this product slice.
fix: 1) src/http/invoke.ts: new import `getGrantsForSubject` from `../db/grants-dao.js`. `loadCallerInvokeGrants` signature changes from `(client: pg.PoolClient, tenantId, callerId)` to `(pool: pg.Pool, tenantId, callerId, nowMs: number)` — module-private function, not exported, no external caller depends on the old shape. Body becomes a 2-line delegation: `const grants = await getGrantsForSubject(pool, tenantId, callerId, nowMs); return grants.filter((g) => g.operation === 'invoke');`. Both call sites (POST /api/invoke/request, POST /api/invoke/command) updated to pass the route's own `pool` closure variable + `nowMs` (already computed) instead of the outer withTenantTx `client` — getGrantsForSubject always opens its own read-scoped tx on the pool, mirroring every other consumer (records.ts's resolveFieldVisibility/resolveReadVisibility, org.ts's capability-token check, capability-grants-dao.ts, sandbox-gate-dao.ts, registry-digest-dao.ts, role-grant-dao.ts). 2) ci/checks/invoke-grant-isolation.sh: additive IG-7 check (header comment + new section before the Result block) — static grep proving invoke.ts uses the shared resolver, not a bespoke query; the check materializes the non-comment file view into a variable before grepping rather than piping `echo "$(...)" | grep -q` directly (avoided a real SIGPIPE/pipefail false-FAIL discovered while writing this check — see friction_events). 3) src/__tests__/invoke-caller-spoof.adversarial.test.ts: recording-stub pool gains 3 new SQL-routing branches matching getGrantsForSubject's 3-step query shape (employee-by-slug / role_assignment-canonical-predicate / grant-with-dual-control), replacing the single old inline-JOIN branch; the existence-check for loadActiveRoleAssignment's branch was tightened (`!sql.includes("ra.role_id")`) to stay disjoint from the new step-2 branch. 4) ci/checks/db/invoke-grant-resolver.db.test.ts: new live-PG test file (4 tests) mirroring the rights-eligibility-sew.db.test.ts / grants-dao-dual-control.db.test.ts fixture pattern.

While writing IG-7 in ci/checks/invoke-grant-isolation.sh, the first version piped `echo "$(noncomment_view)" | grep -qE ...` inside `if ! ...; then`, which under `set -o pipefail` produced a false FAIL (exit 141/SIGPIPE from grep -q closing the read end early on a ~330-line non-comment view, racing echo's write) even though the pattern demonstrably matched. Fixed by materializing the non-comment view into a shell variable first and grepping a here-string (`grep -qE ... <<< "$VAR"`) instead of piping through echo — no pipe, no SIGPIPE race. Re-verified green post-fix and mutation-tested (temporarily restored pre-fix invoke.ts — all 3 IG-7 sub-checks correctly failed; restored fix — green again).
